newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin works on CIS issues while on holiday.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin works on CIS issues while on holiday.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin, who is on holiday in the Black Sea resort of Sochi, on Sunday worked on documents concerning Russia's relations with other former Soviet republics in the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS).

His press service said in a statement that Yeltsin had written to Belarus' President Alexander Lukashenko to express support for closer cooperation between their two countries, Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan.
The four republics share a customs agreement.

Russia and Belarus also signed a Union Treaty earlier this month, though its provisions were watered down at the last minute due to pressure from Russian liberals worried by Lukashenko's distaste for capitalism and authoritarian rule.

The presidents of two other former Soviet republics, Ukraine and Moldova, will join Yeltsin in Moscow on May 8 for the signing of a memorandum on the normalisation of ties between Moldova and its breakaway Dnestr region, the press service said.
Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov brokered an agreement between Moldova and its Russian- and Ukrainian-speaking rebels earlier this month.
Rebel leaders and representatives of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) will also attend the signing ceremony, the press service said.

Yeltsin, who arrived in Sochi on Friday after a three-day visit to Germany, is expected to stay in the resort for about 10 to 12 days but will briefly interrupt his holiday on Tuesday to host Chinese President Jiang Zemin in Moscow.
Chief Kremlin doctor Sergei Mironov told Itar-Tass news agency on Friday that the 66-year-old leader's rest was "not linked to medical necessity" and no special medical treatment was planned.

Yeltsin, who had major heart surgery in November and pneumonia in January, looked pale and tired after talks on Thursday with Chancellor Helmut Kohl, his personal friend and political ally, in the spa resort of Baden-Baden.
